objects.description: Namespace-scope constexpr integer constant indicating the assumed size of an L1 cache line for the target architecture. Used for alignment and padding decisions in lock-free data structures. Value is selected per-architecture: typically 64, but 128 on powerpc64 and 256 on s390x per the header’s branches.

Namespace-scope constexpr aliases for common std::memory_order values to shorten code at call sites: A (acquire), R (release), X (relaxed), C (seq_cst), AR (acq_rel). They are constants of type std::memory_order.

A lightweight barrier/synchronization primitive in namespace atomic_queue. Internally maintains an atomic unsigned counter. Threads call wait() to announce arrival and spin until the counter becomes zero; a coordinating thread calls release(expected_counter) to wait until the counter reaches the expected value and then resets it to zero, releasing the waiting threads. Likely intended for short spinning with spin_loop_pause() hints. No ownership semantics beyond regular automatic or dynamic storage; no copying/moving is defined (implicitly generated). Note: exact semantics and required expected_counter usage are inferred from the implementation; detailed usage protocol is not documented here.

A thin RAII-friendly wrapper over POSIX pthread spin locks. Non-copyable. Provides lock/unlock and a scoped_lock alias to std::lock_guard<Spinlock>. Constructor initializes pthread_spinlock_t and aborts on failure; destructor destroys it.

A fair ticket-based spinlock that uses two cache-line-aligned atomics (ticket_ and next_) to provide FIFO acquisition. Provides nested LockGuard for RAII and exposes it as scoped_lock. Non-copyable. lock() returns the acquired ticket number; unlock() can be called with or without that ticket.
RAII helper for TicketSpinlock. Acquires a ticket on construction and releases it on destruction using the stored ticket number. Non-copyable.

A simple test-and-set spinlock with no fairness guarantees. Uses an atomic<unsigned> flag and pause-based spinning. Non-copyable. Provides lock/unlock and a scoped_lock alias to std::lock_guard<UnfairSpinlock>.

functions.name: atomic_queue::spin_loop_pause
functions.signature: static inline void spin_loop_pause() noexcept
functions.description: Architecture-specific hint to pause/yield during a busy-wait (spin) loop. On x86 it issues _mm_pause; on ARM/AArch64 it emits yield (or equivalent); on other supported architectures it emits a suitable pause/nop sequence, and may be a no-op on unknown targets. Intended to be called inside tight polling loops to reduce power consumption and contention and improve SMT fairness. No return value and guaranteed not to throw.
requirements: No preconditions; may be called from any thread.
Has effect dependent on the target architecture; may be a no-op on some platforms.
Intended usage is inside busy-wait loops; calling outside a spin loop has no functional effect beyond a small delay.

functions.name: atomic_queue::Barrier::wait
functions.signature: void atomic_queue::Barrier::wait() noexcept
functions.description: Increments the barrier’s internal counter, then busy-waits until the counter becomes 0. Intended for threads that must wait until a coordinating thread calls release with an expected counter equal to the number of wait calls since the last release. Non-throwing and uses spinning (no blocking OS wait). Memory ordering: fetch_add uses acquire; the spinning loop uses relaxed loads; release uses a release store to 0.
requirements: Must be paired with a matching call to atomic_queue::Barrier::release on the same Barrier instance; otherwise callers will spin indefinitely.

All participating threads must agree on the expected number of waiters for a given barrier phase; the releaser must pass that exact count to release, matching the number of wait() calls since the last release, or deadlock/spin will occur.
Do not destroy the Barrier object while any thread is inside wait() or release().
This is a spin-wait; callers should ensure conditions that avoid unacceptable CPU burn (e.g., use when the wait is expected to be short or on dedicated threads).
Thread-safety: Multiple threads may call wait() concurrently on the same Barrier instance.

functions.name: atomic_queue::Barrier::release
functions.signature: void atomic_queue::Barrier::release(unsigned expected_counter) noexcept
functions.description: Blocks (spins) until the internal counter equals expected_counter, then atomically sets the counter to 0 with release semantics, unblocking threads waiting in wait(). Used by a coordinating thread after the required number of threads have called wait() for the current barrier phase.
requirements: expected_counter must equal the number of calls to wait() since the previous successful release() on the same Barrier; otherwise release() may spin indefinitely and waiters may never proceed.
May be called by a different thread than the waiters, but must operate on the same Barrier instance.
Do not destroy the Barrier object while release() is spinning or while other threads are in wait().
Non-throwing and spin-based; callers should ensure it is acceptable to busy-wait until the expected count is reached.
expected_counter is an unsigned value; passing 0 is allowed but only meaningful if no threads have called wait() since the last release.

functions.name: atomic_queue::Spinlock::Spinlock
functions.signature: atomic_queue::Spinlock::Spinlock() noexcept
functions.description: Constructs a Spinlock wrapper around a pthread spin lock. Initializes the underlying pthread_spinlock_t; on initialization failure the process aborts. Use to protect short critical sections with busy-wait locking.
requirements: Must be called to create a Spinlock object before calling lock()/unlock().
Construction is non-throwing; on initialization failure the program aborts (no recovery path).
No explicit attributes required from callers beyond normal object lifetime management.

functions.name: atomic_queue::Spinlock::~Spinlock
functions.signature: atomic_queue::Spinlock::~Spinlock() noexcept
functions.description: Destroys the Spinlock and releases its underlying pthread spin lock resources. Calls pthread_spin_destroy; on failure the process aborts.
requirements: The spin lock must not be held by any thread at destruction time (destroying a locked pthread spin lock is undefined).
Destruction is non-throwing; on destruction failure the program aborts.

functions.name: atomic_queue::Spinlock::lock
functions.signature: void atomic_queue::Spinlock::lock() noexcept
functions.description: Acquires the spin lock, blocking (busy-waiting) until it becomes available. On pthread_spin_lock failure, aborts the process.
requirements: The Spinlock object must have been successfully constructed and not yet destroyed.
Must be paired with a matching unlock() by the same thread to avoid deadlock and resource leaks.
May be called concurrently by multiple threads on the same Spinlock; re-entrancy by the same thread is not supported (would deadlock).

functions.name: atomic_queue::Spinlock::unlock
functions.signature: void atomic_queue::Spinlock::unlock() noexcept
functions.description: Releases the spin lock previously acquired by lock(). On pthread_spin_unlock failure, aborts the process.
requirements: Must be called by the thread that currently holds the lock acquired via lock().
The Spinlock must be in the locked state by the calling thread; unlocking an unlocked or foreign-owned lock is undefined.
Must be paired with a prior successful lock().

functions.name: atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::LockGuard::LockGuard
functions.signature: atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::LockGuard::LockGuard(atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock& m) noexcept
functions.description: RAII guard for TicketSpinlock. Acquires the lock on construction using TicketSpinlock::lock() and stores the acquired ticket; the corresponding unlock(ticket) is invoked on destruction.
requirements: The referenced TicketSpinlock must outlive the LockGuard instance.
Construction is non-throwing; it will busy-wait until the lock can be acquired.
Do not manually call unlock() on the TicketSpinlock for the same critical section while the LockGuard is active; the guard will release it on destruction.

functions.name: atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::LockGuard::~LockGuard
functions.signature: atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::LockGuard::~LockGuard() noexcept
functions.description: Releases the TicketSpinlock held by this guard by calling unlock(ticket) with the ticket acquired at construction.
requirements: The associated TicketSpinlock must still be valid at destruction time.
Destruction must occur once per guard; do not attempt to transfer or duplicate ownership (copy/move is disabled).

functions.name: atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::TicketSpinlock
functions.signature: atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::TicketSpinlock() noexcept
functions.description: Default constructor for a ticket-based spin lock. Initializes internal atomics (ticket_ and next_) to zero, establishing an unlocked state.
requirements: Object must be constructed before any lock/unlock operations.
Non-copyable; do not attempt to copy or assign.

functions.name: atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::lock
functions.signature: unsigned atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::lock() noexcept
functions.description: Acquires the ticket spin lock using a fair ticketing scheme. Returns the caller’s ticket value and busy-waits until next_ reaches this ticket, then enters the critical section.
requirements: The TicketSpinlock must be valid and constructed.
Caller must eventually release the lock, either by calling unlock() or unlock(ticket) with the returned ticket.
Not re-entrant: the same thread calling lock() again without unlocking will deadlock.

functions.name: atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::unlock
functions.signature: void atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::unlock() noexcept
functions.description: Releases the ticket spin lock owned by the caller by advancing next_ based on the current next_ value. Convenience wrapper that reads the current next_ and forwards to unlock(next_ + 1).
requirements: Must only be called to release a lock previously acquired by lock() for the current critical section.
The TicketSpinlock must be valid and constructed.

functions.name: atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::unlock
functions.signature: void atomic_queue::TicketSpinlock::unlock(unsigned ticket) noexcept
functions.description: Releases the ticket spin lock corresponding to the provided ticket by setting next_ to ticket + 1 with release semantics. Intended to be used with the exact ticket returned by lock().
requirements: ticket must be the exact value returned by the preceding call to lock() for the critical section being ended.
The TicketSpinlock must be valid and constructed.
Do not pass arbitrary or stale ticket values; doing so can corrupt lock state or break mutual exclusion.

functions.name: atomic_queue::UnfairSpinlock::lock
functions.signature: void atomic_queue::UnfairSpinlock::lock() noexcept
functions.description: Acquires a simple, potentially unfair spin lock using an atomic exchange. Busy-waits until the lock becomes available.
requirements: The UnfairSpinlock must be valid and not destroyed.
Must be paired with a matching unlock() by the same thread.
Not re-entrant: locking twice from the same thread without unlocking will deadlock.

functions.name: atomic_queue::UnfairSpinlock::unlock
functions.signature: void atomic_queue::UnfairSpinlock::unlock() noexcept
functions.description: Releases the unfair spin lock by storing 0 with release semantics.
requirements: Must be called by the thread that currently holds the lock acquired via lock().
The UnfairSpinlock must be in the locked state by the calling thread; unlocking an unlocked or foreign-owned lock is undefined.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueMutexT::try_push
functions.signature:
template<class T, class Mutex, unsigned SIZE, bool MINIMIZE_CONTENTION, class U>
bool atomic_queue::AtomicQueueMutexT<T, Mutex, SIZE, MINIMIZE_CONTENTION>::try_push(U&& element) noexcept
functions.description: Attempts to enqueue one element into the bounded queue. Acquires the internal mutex, checks capacity, and if not full assigns the provided value into the next slot and advances the head. Returns true on success, false if the queue is full. Intended for concurrent producers/consumers; the method handles its own locking. Note: the function is declared noexcept; if assigning/converting U into T throws, the program will call std::terminate.
requirements: Template parameter SIZE must be greater than 0 (array q_[size_] requires a positive size).
Type T must be assignable from U&& (q_[...]=std::forward<U>(element) must be well-formed).
The assignment/conversion from U to T should not throw; if it throws, noexcept is violated and std::terminate will be called.
Queue instance must be a valid, live object when called.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads; internal mutex ensures mutual exclusion.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueMutexT::try_pop
functions.signature:
template<class T, class Mutex, unsigned SIZE, bool MINIMIZE_CONTENTION>
bool atomic_queue::AtomicQueueMutexT<T, Mutex, SIZE, MINIMIZE_CONTENTION>::try_pop(T& element) noexcept
functions.description: Attempts to dequeue one element from the bounded queue. Acquires the internal mutex, checks if the queue is non-empty, moves the next value into the provided reference, advances the tail, and returns true. Returns false if the queue is empty and leaves element unmodified. Intended for concurrent producers/consumers; the method handles its own locking. Note: the function is noexcept; if T’s move-assignment throws, the program will call std::terminate.
requirements: Template parameter SIZE must be greater than 0 (array q_[size_] requires a positive size).
Parameter element must be a valid lvalue reference to T ready to receive a value.
Type T must be move-assignable (element = std::move(q_[...]) must be well-formed).
The move-assignment into element should not throw; if it throws, noexcept is violated and std::terminate will be called.
Queue instance must be a valid, live object when called.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads; internal mutex ensures mutual exclusion.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueMutexT::was_empty
functions.signature:
template<class T, class Mutex, unsigned SIZE, bool MINIMIZE_CONTENTION>
bool atomic_queue::AtomicQueueMutexT<T, Mutex, SIZE, MINIMIZE_CONTENTION>::was_empty() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns whether the queue was empty at the moment of the check, based on current head and tail counters. This method does not take the internal mutex and performs a simple check (static_cast<int>(head_ - tail_) <= 0). Intended primarily for observational or single-threaded checks; using it concurrently with push/pop without external synchronization can cause a data race and undefined behavior.
requirements: May only be called without concurrent calls to try_push/try_pop on the same instance unless the caller externally synchronizes access; the method does not lock and reads non-atomic state.
Queue instance must be a valid, live object when called.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueMutexT::was_full
functions.signature:
template<class T, class Mutex, unsigned SIZE, bool MINIMIZE_CONTENTION>
bool atomic_queue::AtomicQueueMutexT<T, Mutex, SIZE, MINIMIZE_CONTENTION>::was_full() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns whether the queue was full at the moment of the check, based on current head and tail counters compared to capacity (static_cast<int>(head_ - tail_) >= static_cast<int>(size_)). This method does not take the internal mutex; it is suitable for single-threaded status checks. Using it concurrently with push/pop without external synchronization can cause a data race and undefined behavior.
requirements: May only be called without concurrent calls to try_push/try_pop on the same instance unless the caller externally synchronizes access; the method does not lock and reads non-atomic state.
Queue instance must be a valid, live object when called.

functions.name: atomic_queue::details::round_up_to_power_of_2
functions.signature: constexpr std::uint32_t atomic_queue::details::round_up_to_power_of_2(std::uint32_t a) noexcept
functions.description: Returns a rounded-up power-of-two value based on a 32-bit unsigned input. Uses a branchless bit-spreading trick to compute the next power of two greater than or equal to a. If a is already a power of two, it returns a. If a is 0, the function returns 0 due to unsigned wraparound in the algorithm.
requirements: Argument a is a 32-bit unsigned integer.
For a == 0, the function returns 0 (this is the implemented behavior).

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon::try_push
functions.signature: template<class Derived> template<class T> ATOMIC_QUEUE_INLINE bool atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon<Derived>::try_push(T&& element) noexcept
functions.description: Non-blocking push attempt. Reserves a slot by advancing the head atomically (with SPSC or MPMC path) only if the queue was not full, and then delegates the actual element placement to Derived::do_push. Returns true on success, false if the queue appears full at the time of attempt.
requirements: Must be called on a properly constructed queue object.
The element must be convertible/assignable to the derived queue’s value_type (Derived::do_push expects a compatible type).
Thread-safety: designed for concurrent use per the queue’s SPSC or MPMC mode; no external synchronization is required by the caller.
On false return, the element was not enqueued and the caller may retry.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon::try_pop
functions.signature: template<class Derived> template<class T> ATOMIC_QUEUE_INLINE bool atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon<Derived>::try_pop(T& element) noexcept
functions.description: Non-blocking pop attempt. Reserves a slot by advancing the tail atomically (with SPSC or MPMC path) only if the queue was not empty, then fetches the element via Derived::do_pop and stores it into element. Returns true on success, false if the queue appears empty at the time of attempt.
requirements: Must be called on a properly constructed queue object.
The output parameter element must be an lvalue reference to a type compatible with the derived queue’s value_type.
Thread-safety: designed for concurrent use per the queue’s SPSC or MPMC mode; no external synchronization is required by the caller.
On false return, no element is written to element and the caller may retry.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon::push
functions.signature: template<class Derived> template<class T> ATOMIC_QUEUE_INLINE void atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon<Derived>::push(T&& element) noexcept
functions.description: Blocking push that always reserves a slot (advances head) and then enqueues the element via Derived::do_push. In MPMC mode, uses fetch_add for FIFO/total ordering semantics as configured. This call does not report fullness; it is expected that Derived::do_push will spin as needed until a slot is available.
requirements: Must be called on a properly constructed queue object.
The element must be convertible/assignable to the derived queue’s value_type.
May spin internally until space becomes available; caller should avoid calling in contexts where spinning is unacceptable.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon::pop
functions.signature: template<class Derived> ATOMIC_QUEUE_INLINE auto atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon<Derived>::pop() noexcept
functions.description: Blocking pop that always reserves a slot (advances tail) and then dequeues via Derived::do_pop, returning the value. In MPMC mode, uses fetch_add for FIFO/total ordering semantics as configured. This call may spin internally until an element becomes available.
requirements: Must be called on a properly constructed queue object.
Return type is the derived queue’s value_type (inferred from Derived::do_pop).
May spin internally until an element is available; caller should avoid calling in contexts where spinning is unacceptable.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon::was_empty
functions.signature: template<class Derived> ATOMIC_QUEUE_INLINE bool atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon<Derived>::was_empty() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns whether the queue was observed empty at the instant of atomically reading head and tail. This is a snapshot and can be stale immediately after return in concurrent scenarios.
requirements: Callable on a const-qualified queue instance.
Return is a best-effort instantaneous observation; caller must not assume it remains true after return under concurrency.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon::was_full
functions.signature: template<class Derived> ATOMIC_QUEUE_INLINE bool atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon<Derived>::was_full() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns whether the queue was observed full at the instant of atomically reading head and tail relative to capacity(). Snapshot semantics only; can change immediately after return.
requirements: Callable on a const-qualified queue instance.
Return is a best-effort instantaneous observation; caller must not assume it remains true after return under concurrency.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon::was_size
functions.signature: template<class Derived> ATOMIC_QUEUE_INLINE unsigned atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon<Derived>::was_size() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the observed number of elements in the queue from a single snapshot of head and tail. If underflow is observed (due to concurrent pops), clamps to 0. Snapshot semantics only.
requirements: Callable on a const-qualified queue instance.
The value reflects an instantaneous observation and may be stale immediately after return.

functions.name: atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon::capacity
functions.signature: template<class Derived> ATOMIC_QUEUE_INLINE unsigned atomic_queue::AtomicQueueCommon<Derived>::capacity() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the fixed capacity (size_) of the derived queue implementation.
requirements: Callable on a const-qualified queue instance.
Derived must expose a member size_ (fulfilled by provided implementations).
